title: converge-sdks-backoff-telemetry-ux
author: Ava Chen
description: Context and motivation: This PR brings a cross-SDK convergence change set across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs to standardize backoff semantics, emit richer retry/streaming telemetry events, and smooth a few ergonomic rough edges in stream consumers. The goal is parity for default retry behavior (exponential+jitter with an optional max_elapsed config), clearer telemetry for upstream callers to reason about retries and resumptions, and small UX improvements that avoid surprising edge cases observed in recent incidents. Primary user-facing improvements: (1) unified default backoff parameters and an explicit opts.backoffConfig/BackoffConfig typed object in all SDKs; (2) new telemetry hooks that emit structured retry/stream events (retry_attempt, retry_backoff_ms, stream_resume_token, stream_graceful_fallback) which are lightweight and safe to enable in production; (3) TypeScript: introduce async iterator helper that returns a single unified StreamResult shape and avoids orphaned promise rejections when consumers bail early; (4) Python: contextmanager for streaming responses so that KV cache and network resources are deterministically released; (5) Go: connection pooling opt-in flag and graceful drain on iterator Close to reduce spurious reconnect storms during scale-downs. Non-goals: changing server-side protocol or adding new server features. Implementation notes and trade-offs: to keep runtime overhead minimal, telemetry events are emitted through the existing metrics bridge with a new compact schema (no heavy JSON payloads) and a per-client sampling rate controlled by client options. Backoff defaults were chosen based on analysis of production latency distributions in ENG-3392 and tuned to avoid excess amplification during transient infra blips. Rollout plan: roll out SDK versions to registries behind feature flags and flip defaults in minor release after a canary week. See linked Linear tasks for rollout tracking.
commits: 3 commits: 1) sdk: introduce shared backoff types + default param docs; 2) telemetry: emit retry and stream lifecycle events; 3) ergonomics: stream helpers (ts async iterator, py context manager, go Close/Drain behavior) + tests
review_thread: Diego: Can we keep the old backoff knobs for opt-in compat? -- Ava: preserved legacy alias BackoffOptions in each SDK; default resolves to unified BackoffConfig. Priya: TS iterator may hide errors if users only await forEach; please add explicit terminal error propagation. -- Ava: added terminal error propagation test and updated iterator docs. Liam: Go Close/Drain needs a test for concurrent Close+Send; added a small concurrency stress test and fix in stream.go. Diego: approve after tests pass. CI: initial Linux unit matrix flaky on py streaming test (redis fixture); reran, green. Final: squash+merge with release notes prepared.
ci_checks: ci/unit (linux, macos): pass; ci/integration (canary network): pass; ci/lint: pass; ci/telemetry-smoke: pass (sampler enabled); flaky: none after rerun
release_notes: Unified SDK backoff defaults and telemetry: user-visible SDKs (python/typescript/go) gain BackoffConfig types, new lightweight retry/stream telemetry events, stream ergonomics helpers (py context manager, ts async iterator, go Close/Drain). Backward compatible aliases preserved. Bumped SDK minor versions across the board.
notes_for_backport: Backport to release/1.9.x: telemetry schema change is additive and safe; prefer to only backport backoff param docs for stability. Backport should skip examples and ci changes.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for backoff math (edge cases: max_elapsed, zero-retries), streaming resume/close semantics, and integration test covering one-minute canary workload with injected transient errors. All tests passing in CI.
notes_from_author: Keep an eye on telemetry volume if you enable full sampling in high-throughput clients; default sampling is conservative. If maintainers want a more aggressive backoff for low-latency but high-error environments, use client opts to set initial_delay and multiplier.
manual_steps_to_validate: 1) install SDK from branch (pip/npm/go); 2) run examples/py/stream_context_example.py to observe deterministic Close behavior; 3) run examples/ts/streaming-consumer and cancel early to ensure no unhandled promise rejections; 4) run sdk-test/integration/stream-retry.spec.ts against canary env
